body:
New minimal per-binding type tracking in emitExpr (exprType typeI32/typeString + a types []exprType slice threaded alongside depth). A Let records its Bound's inferred type; MATCH's own Subject (emitStringSubject) now accepts a LetRef/MAGNET resolving to a typeString binding, not only a bare StringLit -- closes the restriction S222-09 left as a follow-up. A LetRef resolving to typeI32 stays a real, honest error, not silently coerced. Verified end-to-end: LET "cat" (MAGNET MATCH ^cat$) ? S1 : S0 compiles and runs, matching. Lambda's own parameter stays typeI32 always (real type unknowable until Call time) -- named, separate follow-up. 2 new real emitter tests. 70 tests total, GOWORK=off go build/vet/test ./... clean. commit a208d0e.

⚓ ☃
title: MATCH's Subject can be a Let-bound String
